subject: Code for running parallel chains (rstan in Windows)

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Code for running parallel chains (rstan in Windows)
parts:
Hi all,

I noticed there is nothing in the documentation for running parallel chains in Windows.  I thought I would share some code to run multiple STAN chains in parallel in a Windows environment.  Has worked well for me on Win 7 Pro.

Enter code here...
library(parallel)
f1 <- stan(model_code=test_mod,data=data_list,chains =1, iter=1)
CL = makeCluster(4) # set number of clusters = to number of desired chains
clusterExport(cl=CL, list("data_list","f1")) # make data available to rstan in diff cores
clusterSetRNGStream(cl=CL, iseed=4321)
sflist1 <- clusterEvalQ(CL, {
  library(rstan)
  sm<-stan(fit = f1, data = data_list,
           chains = 1, iter=2000)
  return(sm)
})
fit <- sflist2stanfit(sflist1) # group output from each core into one list
stopCluster(CL)


Hope it is helpful,

Matt

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Code for running parallel chains (rstan in Windows)
parts:
Thanks.  We are not experts on using all types of parallel methods and that is why rstan does not use any parallel by default. 

I think the proposed method would work.  But there is one issue I haven't figured out. I guess the code in the OP would use different seed for each chain.  Stan uses its own random number generator and thus ideally we pass the same seed to each chain but set parameter chain_id to be different.  So I guess we need to make some slight change on the code. 

Jiqiang

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Code for running parallel chains (rstan in Windows)
parts:
Thanks again. 

I modified the code a bit so that the seed would be used for each chain though with different chain id.  

library(parallel)
library(rstan)

foo_data <- list(N = 3)
rng_seed <- 234
foo <- stan(model_code = 'data { int N; }  parameters { vector[N] y; } model { y ~ normal(0,1); }',
            data = foo_data, chains = 0)

CL = makeCluster(2)
clusterExport(cl = CL, c("foo_data", "foo", "rng_seed")) 
sflist1 <- parLapply(CL, 1:4, fun = function(cid) {  
  require(rstan)
  stan(fit = foo, data = foo_data, chains = 1, iter = 2000, seed = rng_seed, chain_id = cid)
})

fit <- sflist2stanfit(sflist1)
print(fit)
stopCluster(CL)

Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: Code for running parallel chains (rstan in Windows)
parts:
I tried out the modified code, and it seems to work well.  The only comment I would make is that I like to pull at least one sample before passing the object to the clusters, since rstan's error messages are not passed out of the cluster.  That way you can catch issues with failure to initialize or errors in the data object prior to setting up the cluster.

Matt

parts:
I'm not sure what is going wrong with your code but if you install rstan 2.7.0-2, then you don't need to worry about all these extra lines. You just need to first call

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

or pass cores = 4 to stan().

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Code for running parallel chains (rstan in Windows)
parts:
Also, it's going to take at least as long to run 4 chains
in parallel as it takes to run one chain serially, and probably
longer, because it'll be the max time of running 4 individual chains with
different starting points. And there will be memory contention with
four parallel processes, which may or may not cause a slowdown.

The parallelization doesn't make a single chain go any faster, it just
pushes different chains to different processes (or at least I believe
it's a process-based parallelism behind those R packages).

- Bob
